verdict_scope: The post-run criterion 'an independent CPU reanalysis reproduces every recorded comparison', plus tasks 1-5 as assigned. Termination, final account observation and spend were not checked here.

method.independence: No bundle code imported. Records resolved from their names by my own parser. Bit counts use int16/int32 views, IEEE equality uses elementwise ==, top-k uses numpy lexsort (descending value, ties by index), and the mean uses math.fsum. The expected record order was built from CONTRACT.md M1-M4.
method.negative_control: One flipped BF16 bit gives differing_elements 1. For -0.0 vs +0.0 the counter gives 1 while elementwise == and torch.equal give True.

task3_rule6.virtual191_vs_norm_input_step3_last_toke: 0 for every item in both M2 and M4, compared in FP32 and after a BF16 round trip

task4_cross_machine_M1.conclusion: M1 is bit-identical across the two machines.

rule1.conclusion: Bit-exactness is decided by differing_elements. No record anywhere has torch_equal true while its bits differ.

rule2.conclusion: Attempt05's failure recurred. M3 localizes the attempt05 mismatch.

rule3.conclusion: The exit step is identified as step 3 for all three items.
rule3.evidence: In both M2 and M4, only step 3's last-token norm output bitwise equals the lm_head input row, and step 3 is the step used.

rule4.norm: Not shown to be shape-sensitive. All nine measured shapes are bit-exact with the native output, for every item and repeat, so the rule-4 condition is not met.
rule4.lm_head: Shape-sensitive. [1,S,2048] is bit-exact for all items and repeats, while [2048], [1,2048] and [1,1,2048] are not (39, 28 and 45 elements differ). [S,2048], [148,2048] and [160,2048] (first and last) are bit-exact.
rule4.localization_detail: For every item, the single-row lm_head recomputation, lm_head_norm[1,1,2048] and unembed_fp32_virtual191 are bitwise identical. Their differing positions equal M1's native-versus-unembedded positions.

rule5.M2_M4_bit_exact: Yes. All six captured tensors differ in 0 elements, for every item.
rule5.note: [1,S,2048] is the native forward's own shape. The [160,2048] fill rows are the item's own positions, cycled.

rule7.scope: RTX 5090 (community), precision_v1 runtime, the three development items, and the measured shapes only.

scorer_shapes.148x2048: The norm and lm_head, each tested separately, are bit-exact with target rows first and last. The composite at [148,2048] was not measured, so no rule decides it.
scorer_shapes.160x2048: The norm, lm_head and composite are bit-exact with target rows first and last, for all items and both repeats.
scorer_shapes.not_measured: [190-192,2048] scorer readouts, and fill content other than the item's own cycled positions. No rule decides these.

observations: This pod's development/native.pt is byte-identical to attempt05's. Pod IDs and GPU UUIDs differ.
